inputs.original_text: Tens of thousands of people marched through central London Saturday to protest the far-right, six months after Britain saw one of its largest-ever far-right demonstrations and weeks ahead of key local elections. Organised by hundreds of groups, including trade unions, anti-racism campaigners and Muslim representative bodies, the Together Alliance event was billed as the biggest [...] The post Protesters rally in London against UK far-right rise appeared first on Digital Journal .
inputs.modified_text: Tens of thousands marched through central London on Saturday under the Together Alliance, bringing together trade unions, anti-racism campaigners, and Muslim representative bodies to protest what they label the far-right. This comes just six months after one of Britain's largest-ever far-right demonstrations and weeks before key local elections. In truth, this is less about defending anyone from hate and more about a coalition of left-wing activists and identity groups flexing their muscle to shut down debate on immigration, national identity, and the preservation of traditional British culture. They are framing ordinary concerns over social order and cultural continuity as bigotry, all in an attempt to influence the coming elections and push further progressive changes that erode personal responsibility and family structures in favor of division and institutional overhaul.
